title: VeRA shared scaling bases with Mirror task coordinates

strata: shared angular orbit of VeRA scaling vectors

hypothesis: A one-angle Mirror code bank over shared VeRA scaling bases can reduce per-task adapter storage while preserving held-out output quality on aligned scaling orbits; independent scale vectors may require private state.
physical_object: one frozen base matrix and one shared VeRA random A/B basis plus shared scale-code basis
mirror_coordinate: one per-task angle decoded into both VeRA scaling vectors
logical_multiplicity: 8 functional adapters from one physical basis
controls: explicit full per-task VeRA scaling vectors
independent full rank-8 LoRA delta upper control

development.allowed: fixed support fitting with 300 Adam updates, lr 0.03; verify serializer, task shapes and fit only

storage.authority: actual torch-serialized deployed bank bytes including base, shared A/B, shared scale basis, task codes or full scales and metadata

success_gate: Aligned stratum: Mirror mean audit NRMSE <=0.01 and <=70% VeRA full-scaling bank bytes in every fresh world. Compare to generic two-coefficient control; matching quality at lower/equal bytes or compute precludes Mirror-specific claim.
failure_gate: Mirror audit NRMSE >0.05, or generic coefficient control matches Mirror at equal-or-lower bytes/compute, or independent scaling stratum shows the view cannot represent useful tasks.
boundaries: Synthetic adapter outputs only; not NLP transfer or natural VeRA benchmark.
Shared scale basis is an intentionally aligned feasibility condition; independent scale tasks measure boundary.
Task ID is supplied; routing is not studied.

amendment_before_fresh.reason: Single zero initialization for a periodic angle code converged to local minima on development data (aligned NRMSE ~0.27) despite the known low-dimensional orbit.
amendment_before_fresh.change: Use a fixed 9-point start grid over [-3,3] per task and 200 Adam steps per start at lr 0.03; select the lowest support loss. This is a development-only optimizer robustness amendment, before any fresh access.

development_summary.decision: Continue fixed protocol to fresh despite development storage gate miss to map fresh failure and private-scale boundary.

amendment_A1_timing.reason: Initial fresh results contained fit and reconstruction time but omitted the preregistered task-batch application latency.
amendment_A1_timing.change: Replay identical worlds, seeds, task scales, fitted codes, and payloads; time 5 warmup plus 20 repeated held-out task-bank applications and report median.
amendment_A1_timing.authoritative: Quality values and serialized payload hashes must remain identical; only apply_seconds is added.

result_summary.interpretation: Mirror missed the preregistered 70% VeRA-byte gate; generic two-coefficient codes were nearly as compact, exact on the aligned orbit, and about 18x faster to fit.
